title: Space Dogs
why: Laika is launched on Sputnik 2 on 3 November 1957 with no way of coming back; the film follows her descendants around Moscow.

title: Persepolis
why: Students take the American embassy in Tehran on 4 November 1979 — the revolution turning on the people who made it.
alt: Argo; Howard Carter finds the first step to Tutankhamun's tomb, 4 November 1922

title: Passchendaele
why: The Canadians take what is left of Passchendaele village on 6 November 1917, after three months and a quarter of a million casualties.

title: Rudy
why: Rudy Ruettiger gets on the field against Georgia Tech for the last twenty-seven seconds on 8 November 1975, and is carried off it.

title: Stanley and Livingstone
why: 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?' — Ujiji, on the shore of Lake Tanganyika, 10 November 1871.
alt: The Edmund Fitzgerald sinks, 10 November 1975; Sesame Street's first episode, 10 November 1969

title: In Cold Blood
why: Four members of the Clutter family are killed in their farmhouse outside Holcomb, Kansas, on the night of 14/15 November 1959.

title: The Royal Hunt of the Sun
why: Pizarro takes Atahualpa at Cajamarca on 16 November 1532 — 168 Spaniards against an empire, decided in an afternoon.

title: The Power of the Powerless
why: Riot police corner a student march on Narodni trida on 17 November 1989 and the Velvet Revolution starts that night.

title: Steamboat Willie
why: Mickey Mouse's birthday — the first synchronised-sound cartoon premiered at the Colony Theatre on 18 November 1928.

title: For All Mankind
why: Apollo 12 lands in the Ocean of Storms on 19 November 1969, four months after Apollo 11 and with a much better soundtrack.

title: The Aeronauts
why: The first free manned flight — Pilatre de Rozier and d'Arlandes over Paris in a Montgolfier balloon, 21 November 1783.

title: An Adventure in Space and Time
why: Doctor Who goes out for the first time at 17:16 on 23 November 1963 — the day after Dallas, so half the country missed it.

title: Teheran 43
why: The Tehran Conference opens on 28 November 1943 with Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill in one building — and, in this film, a plot to kill all three.

title: George Harrison: Living in the Material World
why: Harrison died on 29 November 2001; Scorsese's film is built out of what he left behind.

title: Whisky Galore!
why: St Andrew's Day, 30 November — and no film is more Scottish about a cargo of whisky.
alt: The Crystal Palace burns down, 30 November 1936; Churchill born 30 November 1874

title: A Charlie Brown Christmas
why: First broadcast on 9 December 1965, against everyone's advice, with a jazz score and a real Bible reading. Half of America watched.

title: A Beautiful Mind
why: The Nobel Prizes are presented in Stockholm every 10 December — the ceremony the film ends on.
alt: Human Rights Day; The Theory of Everything

title: W.E.
why: Edward VIII broadcasts his abdication on 11 December 1936 — 'the woman I love'.
alt: Goodfellas — the Lufthansa heist at JFK, captioned 11 December 1978; The King's Speech

title: Amundsen
why: Amundsen's party plants the flag at the South Pole on 14 December 1911, thirty-four days ahead of Scott.
alt: Scott of the Antarctic (1948); The Last Place on Earth

title: Gone with the Wind
why: Premiered at Loew's Grand in Atlanta on 15 December 1939, to a city that declared a public holiday and would not let Hattie McDaniel attend.
alt: Walt Disney dies, 15 December 1966 — Saving Mr. Banks

title: Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines
why: Twelve seconds and 120 feet at Kitty Hawk, 17 December 1903.

title: The Nutcracker
why: The Nutcracker premiered at the Mariinsky on 18 December 1892 and was thought a failure. It is now most ballet companies' entire December.

title: Scrooge
why: A Christmas Carol went on sale on 19 December 1843 and sold out by Christmas Eve. Alastair Sim is still the definitive Scrooge.
alt: The Muppet Christmas Carol; A Christmas Carol (2009)

title: Dirty Harry
why: The Zodiac's first killings were on Lake Herman Road on 20 December 1968. Three years later he was Scorpio, and San Francisco had Callahan.
alt: Zodiac (2007), which opens on that exact night

title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
why: Disney's folly premiered on 21 December 1937 and invented the animated feature. Also the winter solstice — the longest night to be lost in a wood.

title: Eyes Wide Shut
why: Christmas week in New York, lit entirely by fairy lights, in the darkest days of the year.

title: Bhutto
why: Benazir Bhutto is killed leaving a rally in Rawalpindi on 27 December 2007.
alt: The Beagle sails with Darwin aboard, 27 December 1831

title: Rasputin: The Mad Monk
why: Yusupov's cellar, the poisoned cakes, the river: Rasputin is killed on the night of 29/30 December 1916.
alt: Nicholas and Alexandra (1971); the USSR founded, 30 December 1922
